title: Flowcharts, Pseudocode and Programming Constructs
intro: A short, self-paced catch-up covering the essential lesson ideas. Check every question, then correct anything missed.

stages.label: Remember
stages.lead: Retrieve two ideas from earlier learning.

questions.prompt: What does sequence mean in programming?
options: Instructions run in the stated order
A branch chooses based on a condition
Input must be validated by a database
questions.answer: Instructions run in the stated order

questions.prompt: Forty images are 200 KB each. How many MB in total, using 1 MB = 1,000 KB?

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the key concepts, visual model and worked explanation.

blocks.title: Sequence
blocks.text: Instructions run in order; arrows on a flowchart show control flow.

blocks.title: Selection
blocks.text: A decision tests a condition and follows one of the branches, often using IF/ELSE.

blocks.title: Iteration
blocks.text: Instructions repeat; a loop can be count-controlled or condition-controlled.

blocks.title: Flowchart symbols
blocks.text: Use terminators (start/end), parallelograms (input/output), rectangles (processes), diamonds (decisions) and arrows. Pseudocode expresses the logic as text.

blocks.title: Visual model · Flowcharts, Pseudocode and Programming Constructs
blocks.caption: In a flowchart use a parallelogram, a diamond, and output with branches; sequence and loops may also be shown.

blocks.title: Worked example · Design a pass/fail algorithm: mark 52 passes when mark >= 50.
blocks.text: Start by reading a mark. Use a diamond decision: is mark >= 50? True branch prints Pass; false branch prints Try again. Both branches lead to End. Pseudocode uses IF, ELSE and ENDIF. For mark 52, the true branch prints Pass.

items: sequence — Executing instructions in a stated order.
selection — Choosing a branch based on a condition.
decision diamond — Flowchart shape containing a condition with branches.

questions.prompt: Which programming construct chooses between alternative branches?
questions.feedback: IF/ELSE makes a decision using a condition.

questions.prompt: Which construct repeats a set of instructions?
Which standard flowchart symbol represents a decision?
questions.feedback: Diamonds show conditions with alternative branches.

stages.label: Practise
stages.lead: Match and reorder before applying the method yourself.

blocks.text: Compare flowchart decisions with conditional branches, and loops with iteration.

questions.prompt: Match each flowchart symbol with its purpose.
questions.feedback: Different standard shapes communicate distinct functions.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a simple pass/fail algorithm.
Trace: x = 3; x = x + 4; print(x). What is printed?
questions.feedback: The second assignment adds four to three before output.

questions.prompt: Which construct would ask again until the user enters a valid password length?
questions.feedback: A loop repeats the prompt, with a condition controlling when it stops.

stages.label: Apply
stages.lead: Predict the Code First result and write one exam-style answer.

blocks.title: Code First · Predict → Write → Test → Improve
blocks.caption: Predict the output. Change fileGB to 8. Identify the decision condition and name one other factor in choosing storage.

blocks.text: Explain the different purposes of selection and iteration in a password-length checker which asks again if too short. [4 marks]

questions.prompt: In the Code First program, fileGB = 12 and freeGB = 10. What is printed?
questions.feedback: 12 GB is greater than 10 GB free space.

questions.prompt: If fileGB is changed to 8, what is printed?
questions.feedback: 8 GB is at most 10 GB and fits.

questions.prompt: If the pass mark is 50 and the learner achieves 52, how many marks above the boundary is this?

writing.prompt: Explain the different purposes of selection and iteration in a password-length checker which asks again if too short. [4 marks]
writing.model: Selection tests length [1] and branches by condition [1]; iteration repeats the input prompt [1] until an acceptable value is entered [1].
checklist: I explained what a condition tests.
I described how selection chooses a branch.
I explained how iteration repeats a prompt until a valid input is entered.

stages.label: Check
stages.lead: Check your understanding and review your mastery result.

questions.prompt: A flowchart rectangle normally represents a process.
questions.feedback: The rectangle identifies a processing operation.

questions.prompt: An IF statement automatically repeats its body until the condition changes.
questions.feedback: IF is selection; repetition requires iteration.

questions.prompt: Pseudocode can express selection using IF, ELSE and ENDIF.
questions.feedback: Pseudocode can represent branches in text.
